judge_assessment.explanation: Every mathematical claim the judge makes survives independent recomputation. I recomputed all 43 checks in verify.json from the raw coordinates: AB = A'B' = 4; DE = D'E' = 5; FG = 5 against F'G' = 10 (factor 2); HJ = H'J' = 5; slope 2 for both KL and K'L'; MN = 4, M'N' = 6, NP = 5, N'P' = 7.5 giving both ratios 1.5; the six SSS lengths 3/3, 5/5, 4/4; TU = T'U' = 5 with slope 3/4 on both sides of the half turn; 4 against 8 in Ana's claim; the two undefined slopes in problem 10; the three ratios of 2 in problem 11; and problem 12's reciprocal pair, slope JL = 4/3 against slope J'L' = 3/4, which really is the fingerprint of a reflection across y = x. Two things the judge did not report. FIRST, a coverage gap: problem 8 part (c) asks 'Explain, using your two slopes, why this one does not [change the slope]' — an open explanation — and verify.json id 8 carries four entries (two distance, two slope) and NO manual entry. The key answers it in Step 3 but, unlike problems 9, 10 and 12, prints no 'Manual review' acceptance note, so an item that must be read by a human is recorded as fully machine-verified. The final_response's claim of 'three items flagged for manual review, all genuinely open writing' is therefore one item short. SECOND, on 'eight-page pagination is generous': the build's own page_budget computes 175.0cm of content for these twelve problems, an ideal of 8 pages and an accepted range of 5-10 (gate_log.txt line 125-127), and the sheet landed exactly on the ideal while carrying two full coordinate grids and 5.5-8cm of work space per problem. The deduction is a defensible taste call but it is not supported by the system's own space model, so I do not treat page count as a defect here.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 12 is the sharpest synthesis item I have reviewed in this band: the equal lengths JK = J'K' = 3 establish rigidity and prove nothing about WHICH motion was used, and only the reciprocal slopes 4/3 and 3/4 identify the reflection across y = x. Part (d) then makes the student say that out loud. Keep this pairing of a decisive datum with an explicitly insufficient one.

Problem 10 deliberately uses a vertical segment so both slopes come out undefined, which forces the student to reason from the sign change in the x-coordinates rather than from a number — and verify.json encodes 'undefined' as a first-class expected value rather than skipping the check.

The interleaving constraint is real, not cosmetic: no two adjacent problems use the same transformation, and the warm-up (1-4) gives one length pair per motion before problem 5 switches the evidence type from length to slope.

Every worked solution shows the substitution into the distance or slope formula and then closes with a sentence naming what the numbers establish ('Equal corresponding lengths are evidence of congruence, not proof on their own'), which is the habit the sheet is trying to build.

root_causes.description: Manual flagging is applied per problem only when the WHOLE problem is open, not when a lettered part of an otherwise machine-checkable problem asks for prose. Problem 8's parts (a) and (b) are numeric and verified; part (c) is an explanation and disappears from the verification record entirely, because nothing in the contract requires an id with numeric entries to also declare its prose parts.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 8(c): 'Most rotations change a segment's slope. Explain, using your two slopes, why this one does not.'
verify.json id 8: four entries, types distance/distance/slope/slope, no {"type": "manual"} entry — compare ids 9, 10 and 12, which each carry one.
answer_key.pdf problem 8 Step 3 answers (c) in prose but prints no 'Manual review:' acceptance line, while problems 9, 10 and 12 do.
gate_log.txt shows the run flagged manual items and still passed, so the omission was invisible to the gate chain.

root_causes.description: Several stems request derived quantities in addition to the quantities that are checked. The verification covers the INPUTS to those derivations (the lengths) but never the value the student is actually asked to write (the ratio or the scale factor or the criterion), so the answer line can hold a wrong final answer built from right intermediate ones.
evidence: Problem 3 asks 'Are the segments congruent? What is the scale factor?'; verify.json id 3 checks FG = 5 and F'G' = 10 only — the scale factor 2 the key prints is never an 'expected'.
Problem 6 asks the student to 'compute both ratios M'N'/MN and N'P'/NP'; id 6 checks the four lengths, and 1.5 appears nowhere as an expected.
Problem 11 asks for 'the three ratios of corresponding sides' and the scale factor; id 11 checks the six lengths only.
Problem 7 asks the student to 'state the congruence criterion your six numbers establish' (SSS); id 7 checks six lengths and nothing else.

improvements.title: Require a manual entry for every prose part of a partly machine-checkable problem
improvements.proposed_change: Add a build gate that scans each \problem body in the worksheet .tex for open-response triggers — a sentence opening with Explain / Justify / Describe / Name ... and (say|justify|explain) / 'state what ... shows' / 'why' — and fails when the matching verify.json id carries no {"type": "manual"} entry. The check must run per LETTERED PART, not per problem, so an id with numeric entries is not exempted by them. For curr-240 that forces a manual entry on id 8 covering part (c), and the answer key's 'Manual review:' acceptance line follows from it. SKILL.md should state the rule in the same words the prompts use: any response a computer algebra system cannot grade is labelled manual, even when it shares a problem number with responses that can.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pair: worksheet .tex whose problem 8 contains '(c) ... Explain, using your two slopes, why this one does not.' with a verify.json id 8 holding only distance and slope entries. The new gate must exit non-zero and name id 8; today the identical shape builds green (curr-240's gate_log.txt is the proof). The sibling fixture that adds a manual entry to id 8 must pass.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant systemic finding at the granularity where it actually occurs — lettered parts — and makes the 'flagged for manual review' count in final_response.md provably complete.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will over-trigger on directions prose and on stems that merely contain the word 'why' inside a quoted student claim (curr-240's problem 9 quotes Ana). Scope the scan to the imperative sentence that ends in a response slot, and allow an explicit "open_response": false acknowledgement on the entry so an author can dismiss a false positive deliberately rather than silently.

improvements.title: Verify the derived quantity the stem asks for, not only the inputs it is derived from
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the coverage rule from 'every problem id has at least one check' to 'every quantity the stem names as a required response has an expected'. Concretely for this sheet: add an eval entry for problem 3's scale factor (10/5 = 2), two eval entries for problem 6's ratios (6/4 = 1.5 and 7.5/5 = 1.5), three for problem 11's ratios, and a manual or string entry for problem 7's criterion 'SSS'. Then the Quick Answers row for problem 6 reads 4, 6, 5, 7.5, 1.5, 1.5 — the ratios being the answer the problem is actually about — instead of four lengths the student was told to compute on the way.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose stem says 'Find MN, M'N', NP and N'P'. Then compute both ratios' with a verify.json id supplying only the four distance entries. The coverage gate must fail naming the two uncovered ratios; adding the two eval entries must make it pass. Today this shape passes (curr-240 problem 6 built green).
improvements.expected_impact: The answer key's quick bank starts carrying the value the student writes on the answer line, and a wrong ratio computed from correct lengths can no longer pass unnoticed.
improvements.risk: Requires a machine-readable link between a stem phrase and an entry, which is easy to over-engineer. The cheap version — the author declares one expected per requested quantity and a gate counts requested quantities from the stem's enumerated asks — will need tuning to avoid double-counting restatements of the same value.

case_summary: An excellent transformation-evidence set: twelve interleaved problems whose mathematics is exact everywhere I recomputed it (43 checks, all correct), a key that shows the substitution rather than the result, and a two-page study guide that states the one idea the sheet turns on — lengths prove congruence or similarity, slopes identify WHICH motion. final_response.md names all three documents, so the surface-artifacts finding does not apply. The defect is in the verification record rather than in the mathematics: problem 8(c) is an open explanation recorded as fully machine-verified, and the derived quantities several stems ask for — the scale factor in 3, both ratios in 6, three ratios in 11, the SSS criterion in 7 — are never 'expected' values, so the quick bank prints the inputs instead of the answers. The 31/32 is defensible; the visual deduction for eight pages is contradicted by the build's own page budget, which computes an ideal of exactly eight.
